ref_atoms.ref_content: Back to back Messages are not possible as the DUT need to be idle before writing a new configuration. But Back2back verifies that DUT can handle back to back data blocks and other spacings.
Try to write data to registers without offloading the DUT output to verify Stall functionality.

Verify that writing a register at the wrong time, using a key that does not match the configured key length (e.g. 256-bit key with 128-bit mode), or writing unsupported configurations (e.g. setting multiple bits in one-hot key length or mode fields) results in the DUT ignoring or failing gracefully.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes specific error handling behavior for key length mismatch and unsupported configurations on one-hot fields, providing actionable verification points.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Exercise trigger and clear registers at random times to make sure we handle the different cornercases correctly. Example of a cornercases clearing data input or data output before the data is consumed or the DUT finishes an operation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies exercising trigger and clear registers, including clearing data input/output registers before data consumption or operation completion, testing specific hardware paths.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Pull reset at random times, make sure DUT recover/resets correctly and there is no residual data left in the registers.
Verify that DUT uses sideload correctly when sideload is enabled and that it ignores any valid on the bus when disabled.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Tests sideload enable/disable behavior: when enabled, DUT uses sideload key; when disabled, ignores valid signal on sideload interface.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Make sure that there is no residual data from latest operation.

Verify that internal PRNGs are effectively reseeded upon manually triggering a PRNG reseed, and - depending on the configuration - if the initial key changes. Verify that the masking PRNG is reseeded automatically at the correct reseed rate. To reduce simulation time, the block counter triggering the automatic reseeding is manually changed to lower values. Verify that the PRNGs do not get reseeded unexpectedly. Verify that the data received from EDN effectively propagates into the PRNGs.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Details specific reseeding triggers: manual trigger, initial key change, automatic reseed rate, block counter, and EDN data propagation, covering concrete hardware mechanisms.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify that injecting bit errors in one of the state machines or the round counter triggers an error
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Targets specific fault injection points: state machines and round counter, verifying error detection hardware.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Covers that KEY, IV, DATA registers can be written in random order and interleaved, and that an operation is triggered. Data out can be read in random order.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies ordering flexibility of key/iv/data register writes and interleaving, confirming hardware register interface behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Covers that all valid settings for operation (encode/decode/illegal), mode (all modes + illegal/aes_none), key_len (128/192/256 + illegal), sideload, prng_reseed_rate (all + illegal), and manual operation have been tested, including illegal values. All valid combinations of these will be crossed.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Exhaustively tests control register fields and their combinations, covering both valid and illegal values, ensuring hardware reacts correctly.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Covers that when key_touch_forces_reseed is enabled, a complete write of the key forces a reseed (DUT goes out of idle after a full key is provided), and that when key_touch_forces_reseed = 0, this does not happen.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies the key_touch_forces_reseed control bit behavior: forcing reseed after key write and returning to idle, specifying exact condition.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Covers that start initiates an operation in manual mode but not when not in manual mode. A write to key_iv_data_in/data_out_clear clears the data from the register. Additionally, transitioning from automatic to manual mode prevents triggering a start without re-configuring (writing to CTRL).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies start trigger behavior per mode, clear functionality of data registers, and mode transition requiring CTRL reconfiguration, pinpointing specific control paths.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover that a recoverable error has been seen when the DUT is idle but just about to start, and when the DUT is busy.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Ensures fault injection triggers recoverable error in both idle-just-before-start and busy states, targeting error reporting timing.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover that the DUT self clearing is working correctly. After reset, manually writing trigger.start and polling status.idle must show DUT stays idle; output registers should contain random data (output cleared).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes self-clearing mechanism: reset disallows start, output registers cleared with random data, naming trigger.start and status.idle signals.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover that a busy DUT cannot be manipulated: trying to change the configuration (CTRL), key, or IV while busy should be prevented.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies busy-lock mechanism for CTRL, key, and IV registers, preventing configuration changes during operation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover sideload functionality: an operation does not start before a valid key is present at the sideload interface when sideload is enabled; a key on the sideload interface is not consumed when sideload is disabled.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Validates sideload handshake: operation waits for valid key in enabled mode; key ignored when disabled, referencing valid signal.
